source.title: Neural Mechanisms of Observational Learning: A Neural Working Model

confidence_rationale: Biological grounding for the scaffold path: a neuroimaging synthesis arguing observational/imitative action acquisition recruits the same fronto-striatal (and dorsal-frontoparietal, cerebellar) machinery as trial-and-error learning, so a developmental-scaffold/imitation route to REE's actor-critic substrate is biologically faithful rather than an ad-hoc engineering shortcut. Confidence moderate: it is a review (not a single strong causal study), and it flags an inverted ventral-striatal observational prediction-error that complicates naive transfer.
failure_signatures: The ventral striatum shows an INVERTED coding pattern for observational prediction errors relative to individually-experienced reward prediction errors (Burke et al.), so observational and first-person RL are not simply the same computation with a different input -- naive 'imitation reuses the RPE teacher unchanged' is too strong.

The review draws on healthy-adult neuroimaging (correlational BOLD), not lesion/electrophysiology or developmental data, so the causal necessity of the fronto-striatal pathway for observational action acquisition is asserted rather than demonstrated.

It distinguishes imitation (replicating observed actions WITHOUT outcome processing) from observational learning (processing others' action-outcome contingencies) -- REE's behavior-cloning arms are the former, so the review's outcome-processing observational-learning findings map only partially onto the BC result.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Observational and trial-and-error learning share neural systems: regardless of whether stimulus-response associations are acquired by observation or by direct experience, a dorsal-frontoparietal, a fronto-striatal, and a cerebellar network are recruited at acquisition; a three-phase working model (observation / acquisition / response) organises the observational-learning circuitry, with the ventral striatum carrying observational prediction errors (inverted relative to first-person reward signals).
mapping.ree_translation: Biological warrant for the scaffold build target. The MECH-457 autopsy names 'developmental scaffolding (innate approach + curriculum + imitation)' as a stripped dependency; this review says observational/imitative action acquisition in biology recruits the SAME fronto-striatal actor-critic machinery REE's substrate models, so bootstrapping REE's dorsal-striatal-analog policy from an expert (the 748/749 BC arms; a curriculum/imitation scaffold going forward) is faithful to how brains actually acquire action, not an engineering hack. Consistent with the project's biology-before-formalism design constraint.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is correlational human neuroimaging, and the inverted ventral-striatal observational prediction-error means the imitation route is NOT a trivial re-use of the first-person RPE teacher -- it is a related but distinct computation. The review also separates outcome-processing observational learning from pure action-replication imitation; REE's BC is the latter, so the mapping is partial. Grounds biological plausibility of the scaffold, not a specific algorithm.
mapping.source_context: Human functional-neuroimaging review of observational learning; healthy adult participants; synthesises S-R association, action-observation, and prediction-error findings into a neural working model.

confidence_components.notes: Review-level neuroimaging synthesis, so source_quality moderate (no single causal design). Mapping fidelity moderate: grounds the biological plausibility of the scaffold path but not a build algorithm. Transfer risk raised by the imitation-vs-observational distinction and the inverted observational PE.
